title: Carrot Nose
subject: A girl builds a snowman in the park at lunchtime and ties her crush's lost red scarf on it, hoping he walks past and recognises it
caption: 1968-70 bubblegum pop. Fuzzy combo organ playing bouncy staccato eighth-note riffs, handclaps and tambourine on every backbeat, a round bouncy bass guitar walking in simple root-fifth patterns, straight-eighth drums with a crisp snare. Dry punchy AM-radio studio sound, light spring reverb, slightly compressed mix. Bright unison lead female vocal with a double-tracked octave, simple chanted sing-along hooks. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 120 BPM, G major. Bouncy, sugary and a little cheeky. No strings, no sax, no synths, no autotune, no modern pop gloss, no rapping, no EDM drums.
lyrics:
[Intro - fuzzy organ riff, handclaps, tambourine]

[Verse 1]
Built him a snowman by the park gate
Rolled the middle ball till it weighed a ton
Found a red scarf on the bench last week
His name sewn inside it, in green

[Pre-Chorus]
I tied it round the snowman's neck
Now I'm waiting at the lamppost
Wait, wait, wait

[Chorus]
Carrot nose, carrot nose
Tell him it was me
Ooh, I built you in the snow
So he'd stop and say hello

[Verse 2]
Here he comes with his lunch in a bag
Stops and stares at the lump of white
Pulls the scarf and laughs out loud
Says whoever did this got it right

[Chorus]
Carrot nose, carrot nose
Now he's turned around
Ooh, he's got the scarf in hand
Looking round to see who's there

[Outro - organ riff, handclaps, sing-along tag]
Thank you, carrot nose
Thank you, carrot nose
